Topic: Fundamentals of Linear Algebra: From Spans to Bases

Target audience: University students (Introductory Linear Algebra)

Section: section_1 — Prerequisite Refresh: Vectors as Arrows

Lecture lines:
Vectors represent both magnitude and direction.
Add two vectors: tip to tail.
Scale vectors: stretching or shrinking length.
Vector v (2,1) moves East 2, North 1.
Vectors are building blocks of linear space.

Planned animations:
Create a vector Arrow from origin to (2, 2) in #FF5733 color.
Label the vector 'v' near its endpoint in #FFFFFF.
Transform vector 'v' to (3, 1) to show movement.

Section: section_2 — Linear Combinations and Span

Lecture lines:
Linear combination sums scaled vectors.
The Span is the reach of all combinations.
Two vectors span a 2D floor.
Robot movements combine to cover the floor.
Span reveals all reachable space points.

Planned animations:
Create two base vectors 'v' and 'w' as Arrows in #33FF57 and #3357FF.
Show linear combination 'c1*v + c2*w' by scaling vectors.
Fill the resulting spanned area with semi-transparent #808080.

Section: section_3 — Linear Dependence: The Redundancy Rule

Lecture lines:
Linear dependence means redundancy exists.
Dependent vectors share same line or plane.
Redundant vectors add no new directions.

Planned animations:
Draw three vectors where one is a sum of others.
Highlight the dependent vector in #FF0000.
Remove the dependent vector to visualize redundancy.

Section: section_4 — Bases: The Minimalist Toolkit

Lecture lines:
Basis is the minimal spanning set.
Basis vectors must be linearly independent.
Unit vectors (1,0) and (0,1) form a basis.

Planned animations:
Show a set of vectors as a grid in D3 and D4.
Add a checkmark to indicate it is a basis.
Highlight the linear independence of the basis set.

Section: section_5 — Summary and Synthesis

Lecture lines:
Span: the reach of your vectors.
Independence: the efficiency of your set.
Basis: the perfect, minimal tool set.

Planned animations:
Display all section titles in a list format.
Pulse each title one by one to summarize the flow.
Fade all out to black at the end.

Show arrow label 'v' beside the vector in #FFFFFF.
Animate vector v scaling by 1.5 to demonstrate scalar multiplication.

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Vectors represent both magnitude and direction.",
            "Add two vectors: tip to tail.",
            "Scale vectors: stretching or shrinking length.",
            "Vector v (2,1) moves East 2, North 1.",
            "Vectors are building blocks of linear space."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisite Refresh: Vectors as Arrows", lecture_lines)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Create a vector Arrow from origin to (2, 2) in #FF5733 color.

        v_label = Text("v", font_size=24, color=WHITE)
        
        # Group and position
        v_group = VGroup(v_vector, v_label)
        v_label.next_to(v_vector.get_end(), UP, buff=0.1)
        
        self.place_in_area(v_group, 'B2', 'E5', scale_factor=0.8)
        self.play(Create(v_vector), Write(v_label))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FF5733")

        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FF5733")
        self.wait(1)

from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

        lecture_lines = ["Span: the reach of your vectors.", "Independence: the efficiency of your set.", "Basis: the perfect, minimal tool set."]
        self.setup_layout("Summary and Synthesis", lecture_lines)
        
        # Display titles
        titles = VGroup(*[Text(line, font_size=36, color=BLUE_B) for line in lecture_lines])
        self.place_in_area(titles, 'B2', 'E5', scale_factor=0.8)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(self.lecture[0]), Write(titles[0]))
        self.play(Indicate(titles[0]), self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(self.lecture[1]), Write(titles[1]))
        self.play(Indicate(titles[1]), self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(self.lecture[2]), Write(titles[2]))
        self.play(Indicate(titles[2]), self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        
        self.wait(1)
        self.play(FadeOut(titles), FadeOut(self.lecture))
        self.wait(1)
